Farm Attacks

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate the motives behind the often violent phenomenon of farm attacks

Summary:
Since 1990, 3505 farm attacks have been reported in South Africa, with 1741 farm murders. While the figures may seem small in comparison to the general population, one needs to consider the fact tht there are currently only about 35000 commercial farmers in SA. South African farmers are more than double as likely to be murdered than police officers, and four times more likely than the general population. On top of this, a lot of farm attacks are accompanied by extreme violence and torture perpetrated on the victims.

Press Release:


Farm attacks
Since 1990 more than 3500 farm attacks have been reported. These figures represent 10% of all commercial farmers in South Africa. More shocking statistics suggest that a farmer’s chances of being murdered are double that of a police officer. Farm attacks are often associated with extreme levels of violence and brutality. What are the motives behind these attacks? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Voice
The 19th of August 2013. It’s two o clock in the morning. Gerhard and Dawn Ras are fast asleep on their farm in the North West province, unaware that their four dogs had been poisoned and a group of armed men had entered their homestead. The men managed to enter the house but a security door in the passage leading to Gerhard and Dawn’s room finally stopped them. Nothing was stolen during the incident. Gerhard and Dawn were unharmed – they were among the lucky few.

Link Devi
Did you know, if you’re a farmer in South Africa, your chances of being murdered is more than double that of a policeman.

Voice
Over the past 15 years there have been more than 3500 farm attacks reported in South Africa, and 1741 farmers have been murdered on their farms. This year alone has seen 79 farm attacks and 21 farmers murdered. That’s an average of one murder every week.

Sound Up Michael Mlengana
We believe that one of the major causes, one of the major drivers is pure crime, part of the crime that is affecting South Africa.

Voice
Michael Mlengana is the president of the African Farmers Association of South Africa. He says their members are concerned about the high levels of violence, which go hand in hand with many farm attacks.

Sound Up Michael Mlengana
For example one of our members was murdered, it was so vicious, and you wonder can a poor poverty based human being do this, and then you conclude, no, this is done by a person with a criminal intent.

Voice
69 year old Ndiphiwe Maxham’s body was found next to his car on his Eastern Cape farm in April this year. He had been beaten to death and police said nothing was reported stolen at the scene. His family is still too traumatized to speak to Carte Blanche. But Ndiphiwe’s case is another example of a senseless killing, which also goes against the theory that farm attacks are racially motivated.

Link Devi
It’s impossible to do a story on farm attacks without referring to race – are these attacks racially motivated or is it simply opportunistic crime. Your neighbors are far away, there’s no chance of immediate help, nobody can hear you scream.

Sound Up Solomon Makgale
The data that we have, which we’ve analysed by going through each and every docket, does not suggest at all that these attacks are racially motivated. In the majority of cases, it’s just pure crime.

Sound Up Ernst
In many cases the attacker would come and kill some of the workers and the farmer as well. Obviously the majority of farmers or commercial farmers in this country are white, that’s the reality. So you also find that the majority of farm murders are committed against white people, but this is not a thing where white people are being killed and black people are being left out.

Voice
Ernst Roets is the deputy CEO of Afriforum. They are campaigning to have farm attacks and murders declared a priority crime in South Africa.

Sound Up Ernst
We can mention the case in Lindley where Attie Potgieter was stabbed 151 times with garden forks and pangas, in front of his wife and his two-year-old girl. And then the girl was executed and then his wife was executed. We can name cases of people being stuffed in freezers, we can name cases of people being chopped up, there is this huge problem , but it’s as if government is not in the first place prepared to acknowledge the problem, and in the second place prepared to do something about the problem. So we are campaigning to have this crime prioritized and to have more government intervention.

Voice
Since 2007 the SAPS no longer releases separate statistics for farm attacks or farm murders.

Sound Up Solomon Makgale
One can ask the question, why is it that we are not being put under pressure to release crime stats for gang violence, or crime stats for taxi violence?

Voice
Lieutenant General Solomon Makgale is the national spokesperson for the South African Police Service. He says the police view all murders as priority crimes.

Sound Up Solomon Makgale
Murder, or any form of attack that takes place, be it on a farm, in a village, township, urban area, it’s a murder. That’s the type of crime that it is.

Voice:
But how could the police ever ascertain what the real motives behind farm attacks are without analyzing trends and key differences between farm and city attacks.

Sound Up Ernst
The reason why we say farm attacks are unique, is because farmers have a very unique role to play. We have government saying we need to create one million jobs by 2030, but the employers are being killed.

Sound Up Stinnie du Plessis
We weren’t scared, we took no precautions against it. We just lived naively.

Voice
Stinnie du Plessis and her husband Jannie were the victims of a farm attack on the 6th of January 2013. Just after midnight the couple was woken by two armed men standing over their bed.

Sound Up Stinnie
And immediately, they shot Jannie next to me on the bed.

Voice
As her husband lay bleeding on the bed, one of the men ordered Stinnie to remove her pajamas pants.

Sound Up Stinnie
He ordered me to turn around and tied my hands behind my back with a piece of wire. Then he turned me around and raped me.

They dragged my husband into the safe by his feet and closed and locked the door. And then the nightmare in the safe started.

Voice
But the couple’s ordeal was far from over. After forcing Stinnie to show them where they kept their firearms and petty cash, the attackers locked her and the critically injured Jannie up in the farmhouse’s walk-in safe.

Sound Up Stinnie
They dragged my husband into the safe by his feet and closed and locked the door. And then the nightmare in the safe started.

Link Devi
Stinnie was locked inside this safe, with Jannie, who was bleeding to death.

Voice
The couple would spend eight harrowing hours locked up in the safe.

Sound Up Stinnie
We apologized to each other, 40 years of I’m sorry that wasn’t said, Jannie said I must take care of our children, and our grand children, and I tried to keep him positive.

Voice
When they were eventually found the next morning, Jannie was airlifted to hospital. He fought for his life for 19 days, but eventually succumbed to his injuries.

Sound Up Stinnie
I spoke to him a lot in the hospital, he was so heavily sedated that I don’t think he heard me. I kept telling him he can’t leave me. I can’t come back to the farm with all the responsibility alone. I can’t, if they catch these people, fight a court battle alone. He must please stay alive, he must please stay with me. But the lord decided differently.

Voice
Stinnie’s attackers were unknown to her, but it’s often thought that tensions between farmers and their laborers are behind the violent nature of many farm attacks.

Sound Up Michael
And if that relationship is not a relationship in which both people respect one another, you will find a lot of too much pretense, “yes sir, yes baas, yes this”, and you will assume there is respect, but inside the workers are not happy.

Sound Up Lorraine
Devi: In these cases, how many of them knew their attackers?
Lorraine: Just looking at the interviews I’ve done this far, I would say less than 20% of the cases.

Voice
Lorraine Claasen is completing her master’s degree in criminology. She has been interviewing victims of farm attacks from across the country as part of her dissertation.

Sound Up Lorraine
There is a role-reversal taking place between the victims and the perpetrators. The perpetrators are suddenly in control, they’ve got the weapons, and they say what goes. And it’s just an amplified experience for them in having power, and being able to decide who lives and who dies

Link Devi
Prior to 2003 a commando system was in operation, where rural volunteers got together and provided safety and security funded by the Department of Defense.

Voice
But the commandos were disbanded and replaced by a Rural Safety Strategy implemented by the police

Sound Up Ernst
It’s not a bad strategy, it’s about having units, vehicles, in rural areas, patrolling areas, but there’s a huge gap between what the plan says and what’s happening on ground level.

Sound Up Makgale
We are doing what we’ve been asked to do, in accordance with that strategy that has been developed, now instead of saying why is this not working, it’s very easy to now point a finger at the police and say the police are not doing what they are supposed to do. Meanwhile to solve the problem, you need all hands on deck.

Voice
Stinnie’s attackers were both sentenced to 43 years in jail, but she says her once carefree life on Gretna Green has been turned into one of fear.

Sound Up Stinnie
I live behind bars. I have to lock myself in at 5pm because I am scared, I’m also living in prison.

Voice
Despite the constant fear, she’s decided to stay on at Gretna Green, which has also become the final resting place for her beloved Jannie.
Sound Up Stinnie

Sound Up Stinnie
To me it feels as if Jannie is still here. So I can sit by him and read during the day. I can also talk to him, I do that, I know he’s not there. To me it feels as if a piece of him is still here. And to me it was necessary for my healing to have him here on Gretna Green.
